title: bug(plugin-grid): the column-summary percent branch re-spells percentDisplayValue and appends a literal percent sign — it disagrees with the declared source in every non-en locale
body:
`formatSummaryLabel` in `packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts` (the `colType === 'percent'` arm, lines 331-333) holds a **hand-inlined copy of `percentDisplayValue`'s body** and then appends a **literal ASCII percent sign**:

```ts
const decimals = column?.precision ?? 0;
const pct = (value > -1 && value < 1) ? value * 100 : value;
formatted = `${pct.toFixed(decimals)}%`;
```

The right-hand side of line 332 is the expression `percentDisplayValue` in `@object-ui/core` IS, character for character. So the SCALING agrees today — and agrees by duplication rather than by reference, which is the shape objectui#9165, objectui#9071 and objectui#5607 each removed from one other surface. The CONVENTION is not taken at all.

## Why this is a contract violation and not a style nit

`percentDisplayValue`'s own doc comment states the contract, and the sentence is the judgement:

> If a third surface ever needs percent display, it takes BOTH halves from here - the scaling AND the convention - or this promise breaks again in the same place.

A grid column-summary footer showing a percent aggregate is such a surface. It takes neither half by reference: the scaling is re-spelled, the convention is a literal `%`.

## Measured, not inspected

The expression above, copied verbatim out of the source, against `formatPercent(value, 0, locale)` - the list-cell path that reaches the declared source. Both evaluated in the same run, in this repo's runtime:

| locale | stored | column summary | declared source | agree? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `en` | `0.25` | `25%` | `25%` | yes |
| `en` | `1` | `1%` | `1%` | yes |
| `en` | `-5` | `-5%` | `-5%` | yes |
| `en` | `12.3` | `12%` | `12%` | yes |
| `en` | `1234.5` | `1235%` | `1,235%` | **NO** - grouping |
| `de-DE` | `0.25` | `25%` | `25 %` (no-break space) | **NO** - affix |
| `de-DE` | `1234.5` | `1235%` | `1.235 %` | **NO** - affix and grouping |
| `tr-TR` | `0.25` | `25%` | `%25` | **NO** - the sign moves to the FRONT |
| `tr-TR` | `1234.5` | `1235%` | `%1.235` | **NO** - same |

Every `en` row below four digits agrees, which is exactly why a spot check in the default locale reads clean. The scaling column never disagrees - that half is a duplicate, not a drift, **today**.

## The harm class

The same one objectui#4576 measured and paid for: a German session reads `1.234,5 %` from a list cell and `1.234,5%` from the aggregate footer directly beneath it, the same number under two conventions. Turkish is worse than a spacing difference - the percent sign is on the other side of the number. This is the identical harm the three converged surfaces were repaired for; this one was never in any of their scopes.

There is a second, smaller instance in the same function at line 301, the `PERCENT_TYPES` arm (`percent_empty` / `percent_filled`), which also appends a literal `%` to a `toLocaleString` body. It is arguably a different animal - those are computed fill ratios, not a stored percent field - so it is named here rather than assumed in.

## Why it is not a duplicate of the three converged cards

- objectui#5607 moved `recordFields` in `plugin-dashboard` onto the declared source.
- objectui#9071 converged the `plugin-detail` summary chip's scaling half.
- objectui#9165 converged the `plugin-dashboard` metric tile, both halves.
- objectui#9167 holds the remaining convention half for the `plugin-detail` chip.

None of the four names `plugin-grid`, and none names `useColumnSummary`. This surface has never been in scope.

## Suggested route

The same one the other three took: delete the local expression and call the declared source. ⚠️ One thing to decide rather than inherit - the scaling half can be converged on its own with **zero** rendered change (the expression is already byte-identical), while the convention half moves every non-`en` session and four-digit `en` values. Whether both halves land together is the same question objectui#9167 is holding for the chip, and the answer should probably be the same for both.

⚠️ Also worth checking before implementing: `decimals` here reads `column?.precision`, whereas the neighbouring currency arm reads `column?.scale` with an in-code note (#2131) that `precision` is the total digit count of a `decimal(p, s)` column and reading it padded a sum out. Whether the percent arm reading `precision` is the same defect is NOT measured here and is stated as an open question, not as a claim.

## Dedup

Run, and it is a reading rather than a dead channel. Channel: repo-scoped REST issues list filtered to the `domain:ui` label, followed to the end (4 requests, page 4 returned 14, page 5 empty; 314 open issues after excluding pull requests), then a local title-and-body keyword scan. `/search/issues` was probed first and is refused by this container's egress proxy with a path-whitelist message, so it was not used. Controls fired both ways in the same scan: a near-verbatim objectui#9165 title returned exactly 1 hit, and an impossible control string returned 0. Scans: `useColumnSummary` 0 hits, `column summary` 0, `columnSummary` 0, `plugin-grid percent` 0, `summary percent` 0, `aggregation footer` 0; `percentDisplayValue` returned 2, both of them objectui#9165 and objectui#9167. Scope boundary, stated rather than papered over: open issues carrying `domain:ui`; an unlabelled card would not have been seen.

Filed by the `os-dev` seat while implementing objectui#9165, found by a census for the same rule's other spellings. Generated with Claude Code, session `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`. (Attribution written as prose deliberately - a footer block is stripped when an issue is created.)
